query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a small amount of oxygen to the equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy can improve its oxidation resistance without sacrificing its mechanical performance.
generation.intervention: addition of a small amount of oxygen
generation.conditions: room temperature, strain rate of 10−4–10−2 s−1
generation.mechanism: The formation of ordered oxygen complexes can improve the oxidation resistance of the alloy by reducing the diffusion of oxygen into the alloy. This can be derived from materials-science principles and is supported by records W2914703696 and W2754519447.
generation.predicted_outcome: improved oxidation resistance without sacrificing mechanical performance
generation.boundary: temperature range of 500-1000 °C, atmosphere of air or oxygen, exposure time of several hours
generation.uncertainty: the exact amount of oxygen to be added and the optimal processing conditions are unknown

falsification_experiment.design: compare the oxidation resistance of the oxygen-added alloy with the untreated alloy under the same conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the oxygen-added alloy shows no improvement in oxidation resistance, the hypothesis is falsified

Question: Whether it is necessary to use all five elements (Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr) to achieve a random solid solution and good mechanical properties, or if reducing the system to 3 or 4 elements yields similar results.. System: HfNbTaTiZr system; specific alloys: HfNbTaTiZr (5-element), NbTaTiZr, NbTaTi, NbTiZr, TaTiZr, Nb0.5TaTiZr1.5, Nb1.5TaTiZr0.5 (3 and 4-element MEAs).. Processing: Vacuum arc melting in a water-cooled copper crucible; elements with 99.9% purity; ingots cast 8 times and flipped for mixing; no Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) or heat treatment applied to cast material.. Test conditions: Room temperature tensile testing with a strain rate of 2 × 10−4 s−1; Vickers hardness HV30 measurements; microstructure and phase analysis via SEM, WDS, and XRD..
